$comment: Mission 1.76.1. THE REVIEWED INTERPRETATION. The reply is frozen in globalping-r2-provider-reply-v1.json and is not restated here as a source. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS keep R2 open, and either alone would be enough: the sender is not established, and the reply answers the half of the question that was already closed.

source.why_not: two copies of one sentence drift, and the drift is discovered by whoever trusted the wrong one.

question_1_attribution.$comment: Is the reply attributable to an established provider representative?
question_1_attribution.why_it_is_missing: the mailbox is the only surface holding them and the connector in this session refused the read for missing permissions. Nothing was retrieved.
question_1_attribution.why_the_thread_is_not_enough: a reply appearing in a thread is consistent with the provider having sent it and does not establish that anyone at the provider did. R1's author was established from GitHub's own author_association plus an independent public-membership endpoint; nothing of that kind exists for a private email.
question_1_attribution.contrast_with_r1: R1 closed on a raw read of a PUBLIC surface. R2's reply has no public surface, so its provenance ceiling is set by whether the mailbox can be read -- which is the same shape as Mission 1.66's dispatch ceiling, one step later in the conversation.

attribution_levels.OPERATOR_SUPPLIED: a body with no sender, no date and no headers. This.
attribution_levels.RAW_MAILBOX_READ: the message retrieved from the thread, establishing the From address, the display name and the Date. Not reached.

question_1_attribution.why_a_rights_residual_needs_the_higher_l: closing R2 records that the provider permitted commercial measurement of third-party infrastructure. Acting on that permission means directing traffic at other people's servers, so the cost of being wrong is borne by third parties rather than by this project.

question_2_responsiveness.$comment: Is the reply responsive to the FULL question asked?
question_2_responsiveness.what_the_reply_states: that commercial use is allowed, subject to three named limitations. It names neither HEAD, nor targets, nor third parties, nor public reachability.
question_2_responsiveness.the_strongest_argument_that_it_answers_m: a prohibition on using Globalping as a PROXY only makes sense if directing measurements at destinations the user chooses is otherwise contemplated -- you cannot proxy through a service that only measures your own infrastructure. So the carve-out arguably presupposes third-party target use.
question_2_responsiveness.why_that_argument_does_not_carry: it is an inference from a presupposition, and Mission 1.74 already graded exactly that shape as non-closing: the maintainer statement that PRESUPPOSED redirect responses appear in results was real evidence and not a commitment. A presupposition is not a statement, and the discriminator asked for a statement.
question_2_responsiveness.compound_question_note: the question was compound and the answer picked up one clause. That is ordinary correspondence behaviour rather than evasion, and it is the reason a re-ask should isolate the open half instead of repeating the pair.

question_3_does_it_establish_permission.$comment: Does 'yes we allow commercial use' establish permission for the use described?
question_3_does_it_establish_permission.discriminator_frozen_before_the_send: an answer stating that the current Terms do or do not cover measuring third-party publicly reachable targets maps directly to R2-B. A statement that a separate permission is needed maps to PROVIDER_TERMS_REQUIRE_CLARIFICATION rather than to a grant.
question_3_does_it_establish_permission.what_the_discriminator_required: an answer STATING that the current Terms do or do not cover measuring third-party publicly reachable targets
question_3_does_it_establish_permission.so_what_it_adds_to_r2_a: corroboration from a more direct surface than the FAQ that closed it -- a direct answer rather than a published page -- and three limitations the FAQ does not state. Both would be real gains if the sender were established.
question_3_does_it_establish_permission.why_this_is_the_sharper_finding: the attribution gap could be closed by one authorised mailbox read. This one could not: even a fully verified message would still not contain a statement about third-party target coverage, because the sender did not make one.

question_4_limitations_stated_by_the_pro.$comment: Recorded as CLAIMED rather than established, because the speaker is not established. If the sender is later confirmed, these become provider-stated conditions and none of them may be dropped.
question_4_limitations_stated_by_the_pro.why_they_are_recorded_even_at_this_level: a limitation is the part of a permission a reader is most likely to drop, and the moment to write it down is when it is read rather than when it is needed.
question_4_limitations_stated_by_the_pro.what_that_means: 'no abuse' is a standard the provider did not bound, so it cannot be treated as a checkable condition. Recording it as a named limitation is honest; treating it as satisfied would not be.

two_independent_reasons: the sender is not established, so no provider authority attaches to the words
the words, taken entirely at face value, state permission for commercial use and state nothing about third-party publicly reachable target coverage
question_5_does_it_close_the_residual.why_that_matters: a single reason invites the reading that fixing it would close R2. Two mean an authorised mailbox read would establish WHO said it and still leave WHAT they said short of the open half.

question_6_qualification.$comment: Nothing moved, and the tally is restated rather than recomputed.

what_would_close_r2_b.$comment: Named so the next enquiry is one question rather than four.
what_would_close_r2_b.the_open_question: whether the current Terms cover measuring publicly reachable THIRD-PARTY targets, as distinct from 'your internet infrastructure'
what_would_close_r2_b.why_the_last_enquiry_did_not_get_it: the question was compound, and a compound question invites an answer to whichever clause the reader finds easiest. The commercial clause was already settled and it is the one that came back.
what_would_close_r2_b.shape_of_a_follow_up: one sentence naming only the target-scope tension: Permitted Use says 'your internet infrastructure', and the question is whether measuring a website somebody else operates falls inside it. No commercial clause, because that half is closed.
what_would_close_r2_b.why: the v2 approval authorised exactly one send and one was made, so it is spent. A different question is a different action.
what_would_close_r2_b.and_first: an authorised mailbox read would establish who replied, which is worth doing before asking the same correspondent again.

chain.provider_reply: an email reported to be in the GP-R2-Q1 v2 thread
chain.gate_result: no verdict moved; the closure and qualification records are untouched
